body.statement: In the deterministic multitape Turing bit model, can \(\mathsf{FastCert}_n(e,\alpha,\xi)\) be constructed so that, for fixed \(c,K,L_q,L_r,B\), its bit complexity is bounded by a polynomial in \(n\), the total input length \(\Lambda_n\), and \(\xi^{-1}\)? On every feasible input for which \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) returns \(a_n\), it must terminate with \(\widetilde a_n\) satisfying \(a_n\le\widetilde a_n\le a_n+\xi\) and \(\sup_{q'\in\mathcal Q_n(e),r'\in\mathcal R}\mathbb E H_{\widetilde a_n,h_n}(Z_{r',q'})\le\alpha-\Delta_n\). Can this be achieved with the certified pruning invariant in the branch-and-bound handle while retaining the \(13/32\) late-ramp certificate and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard oracle bound, with only \(\xi\) added to a reported computational radius?
body.justification: The exhaustive certificate establishes computability but may be expensive; a complexity-controlled certificate is the first-class unresolved computational-statistical question.
body.gap: Neither classical compound-Poisson approximation nor selective randomization inference gives a polynomial-time outward-rounded optimization over continuous signed profile classes.
body.consumer: A polynomial certificate would make prespecified daily calibration feasible at the GUSTO-1 and EUROPA trial scales.

obligation.what_is_open: A worst-case bit-complexity bound polynomial in n, the encoded input length, and the inverse threshold tolerance for the branch-and-bound certificate over both continuous Lipschitz profile classes.
obligation.obstruction: The certified pruning invariant supplies only a Lipschitz oscillation bound.  It gives neither a polynomial bound on the number of profile boxes that can straddle the acceptance boundary nor a separation margin from that boundary.  In the worst case an arbitrarily large family of boxes can remain undecided at the required outward precision, so the exhaustive termination proof does not imply polynomial bit complexity.
obligation.attempted: Discretize the profiles on the time mesh, use the common-Poisson Lipschitz modulus to prune boxes, dovetail directed convolution refinements, and binary-search the threshold grid.  These steps prove computability and output validity, but the covering number of the functional Lipschitz classes and boundary-straddling boxes is not controlled polynomially by the frozen primitives.
obligation.partial_result: The exhaustive dyadic-grid certificate terminates, is outward-valid, preserves the \(13/32\) late-ramp certificate and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard oracle bound, and yields the proved finite-coverage and oracle-slack theorem.  Moreover, if a fast routine returns any \(\widetilde a_n\in[a_n,a_n+\xi]\) with the stated outward certificate, monotonicity of \(H_{b,h_n}\) preserves coverage and enlarges the reported radius by at most \(\xi\).  What is not proved is a polynomial worst-case bit bound for finding such a threshold.
